market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: India biopesticides: estimates vary widely — $242.16M (2025) to $381.23M by 2030 (9.5%/yr); or $82.2M (2024) to $204.1M by 2033 (9.23%/yr); or a narrower $32.7M (2022) to $68.6M by 2030 (9.7%/yr). Global PGR market: $5.75B (2024) to $14.24B by 2033 (10.6%/yr) on one estimate, though a lower estimate shows just 0.8-1.7%/yr to $39.5B by 2035 — highly methodology-dependent.

market.domesticSlice: India = 2.2% of global biopesticides market (2022). India PGR market: $115.3M (2025) to $204.8M by 2034 (6.58%/yr); India PGR CAGR was +21.9%/yr 2013-2024, the highest globally, forecast to moderate to 12.70%/yr going forward.

structureFacts: India's National Project on Organic Farming (NPOF, since 2004) provides back-ended NABARD subsidies (up to 25-33% of outlay) for biopesticide/biofertilizer production units — 56 biofertilizer units and 17 compost units established under the scheme to date
Growth drivers: regulatory support, export-driven pesticide-residue compliance requirements, scaling public-sector biocontrol capacity, rising organic acreage (notably Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra)

adoptionStructure.note: Not a fixed repurchase-rate category; subsidy-linked institutional buyers (NABARD-backed units) are a structural demand channel alongside direct farmer/distributor sales
